conventions.convention: Coverage is frequentist, with a fixed truth; approximate empirical-ball coverage includes both observation noise and sampler randomness. Exact Bayesian coverage error is retained as a separate baseline.

The calibration score-error budget is integrated over Lebesgue time and ideal noised-posterior marginals; Euler evaluates the score at deterministic times T-kh. The empirical radius is the smallest order statistic attaining cumulative mass at least 1-γ.

The mixture example instead bounds the supremum over time of spatial squared score error under ideal marginals. Its unbounded-loss conclusion requires positive error allowance and a fixed finite J≥2; each constructed chain has finite first moment.

Normalized Lebesgue measure on the 2π-periodic torus makes 1, √2 cos(kx), √2 sin(kx) orthonormal, indexed starting at j=1. Odd m retains complete frequency pairs. All pointwise architecture weights and biases are independent of spatial position.

Training and test input noise in the neural inverse-map question has covariance σ²m⁻¹I_m; test truth and noise are independent of training. This differs from fixed coordinatewise white-noise variance.

Robust ellipsoid recovery uses relative operator perturbations A_p(I+E), with operator norm of E at most ρ_A<1/2. Training uses the unperturbed A_p; the deployed learner does not receive E. White-noise observations live in the product Borel space R^N, with countably many coordinates, rather than necessarily in ℓ².
The scalar conditioning examples use absolute operator discrepancy. The vanishing-conditioning counterexample varies the working operator with the discrepancy radius.
The two-mode sampling calculations concern independent exact posterior draws; a missed atom and Wasserstein distributional error are distinct quantities.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated scalar parameter choices and every integer K≥1, there is a jointly Borel finite score field with integrated score error exactly zero whose Euler terminal law is N(1,K⁻¹) for every observation. With M=K, empirical-ball coverage at truth zero tends to zero, the uniform boundary-margin condition holds with exponent one, and the exact baseline error is strictly less than 3/4.

For every odd m≥3, every N≥1, and every admissible bounded parameter class with a measurable empirical minimizer, the ERM risk is at least R²(3^p-2^p)²/(4·3^{2(p+s)})>0. The same bound holds for every measurable learner in the specified coordinate-free Fourier class. The unrestricted risk tends to zero as m tends to infinity for fixed positive p,s,R,σ, independently of N.

There are admissible fixed one-dimensional separated-mixture parameters such that, for every fixed positive score-error allowance and every fixed finite J≥2, the supremum of the displayed expected fidelity loss over the stated finite-valued Borel score class is infinite for every finite M≥1.

Writing Q=R² min{1,(σ/R)^{4s/(2s+2p+1)}}, there is c_{p,s}>0 such that c_{p,s}(Q+R²ρ_A²)≤𝔅R_N(ρ_X,ρ_A)≤min{R²,2Q+R²ρ_A²} for every allowed training size and truth-law shift radius. For fixed positive p,s,R, risk tends to zero exactly when σ and ρ_A both tend to zero.

In the scalar Gaussian observation model with proper N(0,τ²) prior, the exact posterior is N(a_nȲ,v_n), and frequentist coverage of its central credible interval is the stated difference of standardized normal cumulative probabilities.

concerns.concern: The title says “Finite samples cannot identify every Lipschitz inverse map uniformly,” whereas the Example and Verification construct arbitrary scalar 1-Lipschitz target functions, specifically zero and a tent. No forward-map model identifies these functions as inverse maps. The stated scalar prediction lower bound is sound; the title needs to match that demonstrated scope or the inverse-map interpretation needs justification.

seams_checked.note: The explicit models preserve the distinction between point reconstruction, posterior sampling, and expected test loss. The prerequisite definitions supply no automatic accuracy or train-to-test guarantee, and none is attributed to them.

Checked the continuum EIT existence statement and related finite-sample open question. The batch explicitly distinguishes generalized coordinate/chart lifting from its coordinate-free Fourier architecture and does not transfer the odd-mesh obstruction to EIT or infer sample and mesh rates from continuum approximation.

Finite reverse Euler updates are specified directly. The batch does not infer convergence, regularization, or generalization from finite-depth well-definedness; this agrees with the prerequisite's explicit limitations.

The prerequisite theorem concerns stationarity for an exact MMSE plug-in map under its objective and step-size hypotheses. The batch makes no claim that this supplies posterior sampling, calibration, or a fitted-score guarantee.

The batch explicitly defines exact conditional target scores and approximate Euler samplers. Its counterexamples preserve the prerequisite distinction between approximate guidance and exact posterior sampling; no plugged-in measurement score is silently treated as exact.

The batch specifies observation laws, losses, uncertainty events, and finite evaluation budgets. It does not promote a benchmark protocol or empirical finding to a universal robustness or calibration theorem.

Absolute scalar mismatch and relative ellipsoid perturbations are separately specified. The robust lower bound locally proves equality of the relevant conditional observation laws and a squared-loss bound; it does not overstate the prerequisite metric-loss theorem or identify operator mismatch with prior-support mismatch.
